title: Reduce complete offline export-check time by 7.46% (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

The complete offline `check --check-inputs` command takes 7.46% less median wall time on the recorded 529-file export, from 59.396417 ms to 54.964250 ms. Reuse the open tar and its populated member index during declaration checking. The manifest is still reread and checked against its recorded size and SHA256.

```diff
 check --check-inputs
   hash every payload and validate the complete receipt
-  close, reopen, and scan every header again
+  borrow the checked archive and its existing index
   reread and authenticate the manifest
   validate declarations and close the owned archive
```

Claim type: measured tooling improvement with a scoped stable-input equivalence argument and finite conformance evidence. No new mathematical theorem, native supplier, kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

The [package](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/tree/9889f94b6ed045c1069b2e6f7e4471d0322f2f16/research/export-single-scan) preserves exact source pins, the original CLI scripts, raw timings, the profile and a generated source-bound receipt. Credit Tekalign, Ali Romman, roger-sato, Mihir Srivastava, josecarlosgonzalezroque-design, Douglas Colkitt and the retained exporter/Git-reader contributors. Their original notices remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before range 58.337125–61.354625 ms; after range 53.355958–56.586834 ms. Nine alternating paired batches, five fresh complete CLI processes per side per batch. All nine paired medians improve, all 90 outputs agree, and there are zero errors. Timing includes startup, imports, archive reads, validation and output capture. The archive hash remains unchanged and Git is absent from PATH.
- The primary archive is the official 529-file P104 toolkit export at `a5bff3bf133e482541c09eba4e773884bdb2b1b7`. Its mathematical replay was not run. An untimed profile identifies the second header scan as about 10 ms of a 73 ms profiled command; profiler timings are excluded from the comparison.
- The 82-file, 51-declaration secondary export has overlapping before/after ranges and one losing paired batch. Its timing result is inconclusive. Both workloads together execute 180 successful complete commands.
- Direct normal/optimized conformance passes 44 finite archives and 88 complete outcome comparisons: 67 accepted and 21 rejected pairs. Normal/optimized exporter suites each run 46 tests, with 45 passes and the existing native-Windows-only publication test skipped on macOS. Four added regressions cover single-open completion, exception cleanup, borrowed-handle ownership and actual post-hash manifest mutation.
- All four registered checks pass locally in 0.209, 0.211, 5.713 and 6.616 seconds. Committed bytes, modes and full declared source-history ancestry pass for 22 files. The official export passes integrity and declaration coverage. Normal/optimized direct replay also passes in a read-only Git-free export; source and receipt corruption controls reject under optimization.

## Reproduce

From the repository root with CPython 3.12:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/export-single-scan
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/export-single-scan/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/export-single-scan/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/export-single-scan --check-source-history
```

To repeat timing with fresh external output paths:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/export_research_package.py export --package research/p104-designer-toolkit-v2 --ref a5bff3bf133e482541c09eba4e773884bdb2b1b7 --output /tmp/toolkit-benchmark.tar
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/export-single-scan/benchmark.py --archive /tmp/toolkit-benchmark.tar --output /tmp/toolkit-benchmark.json
```

Any CPython 3.12 installation can replace that interpreter path.

## Limitations

The percentage is a local macOS arm64 measurement with CPython 3.12.15, 18 logical CPUs and concurrent work. The small-file comparison does not establish a useful gain. Stable finite archives are the equivalence domain; the retained reread detects in-place manifest changes, but no filesystem snapshot or concurrent-mutation guarantee is supplied. Native Windows execution, Linux timing, selected scientific replay, predecessor mathematical audits, Lean and Docker are unrun. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No scientific proof obligation is discharged by this transport optimization.

The performance-issue playbook guided the work. Build the Lever produced the reproducible benchmark, Prove It Works required complete-output comparisons, and Power of Ten kept resource ownership explicit and the changed functions below one page.

## Open next questions

Does the same archive-index reuse improve complete-command time on Linux or Windows, or on larger real exports? Start with the pinned official export and the same alternating benchmark. Host measurements are the missing evidence. No further optimization is reserved.

## Related open work

Completion refresh inspected the fifteen other open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM. None studies this offline archive checker or reports a competing result for the same export-check command. No additional predecessor computations were run.

- PR #6199 speeds research-draft creation, a different command and repeated-read cost.
- PR #6203 speeds an affine/vector replay, a different computation.
- PR #6206 speeds the complete H4 support-certificate replay, a different computation.
- PR #6207 speeds a Clifford projection, a different computation.
- PR #5721 changes Windows Git-reader process ownership; this offline checker invokes no Git process.

## CI notes

All three hosted checks passed at exact head `9889f94b6ed045c1069b2e6f7e4471d0322f2f16` in [run 40913005722](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40913005722): `plan`, `replay (research/export-single-scan)` and `replay (research/publication-metadata-reuse)`. The completed checks were read once, and the run's successful conclusion and exact head were confirmed.

Hosted replay certifies the registered checks at this head, including the affected publication-metadata dependent package. The local conformance, publication-byte/source-history, read-only export and corruption checks listed above also passed. The local timing percentage is not a CI performance assertion. No CI failure remains to report. Independent human and formal proof-kernel acceptance remain unclaimed.

The [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19272236) predicted exactly this measured-command scope. Canonical main, priorities, selected bindings, live claims and open/merged overlap were refreshed before publication. Remote overlap pagination was complete; sparse local-note coverage and unpublished work remain limits.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** exporter.

The shared offline checker changes archive lifetime and index reuse. Existing default integrity checks, direct declaration calls and archive bytes retain their contracts. The full exporter suite covers these paths; rollback is a normal code revert.
